server-access.aiToken.badToken: Cannot get a token: the token the issuer gave back does not meet the requirements (owner, AI, scope or lifetime is wrong) and was not handed to the AI; the owner can see why in the audit
server-access.aiToken.beyondOwner: The scope goes beyond what the owner has: {scopes}
server-access.aiToken.beyondOwnerSelf: The scope goes beyond what the owner has: {scopes} (in standalone mode at most {ceiling})
server-access.aiToken.exchangeFailed: exchanging the token with the external issuer failed
server-access.aiToken.grantScope: An AI's token may not carry {scopes}: letting others in belongs to the owner alone
server-access.aiToken.noAccessToken: the issuer gave back no token
server-access.aiToken.noOwnerToken: the owner's token is not stored yet: the owner adds ownerToken when configuring the external issuer (takes the PIN)
server-access.aiToken.notAccessToken: the issuer did not give back an access token
server-access.aiToken.notBearer: the token the issuer gave back is not a Bearer token
server-access.aiToken.notOwner: the stored token is not the owner's own
server-access.aiToken.ownerTokenExpired: the owner's token has expired: the owner signs in to the issuer again, then adds the new ownerToken when configuring the external issuer (takes the PIN)
server-access.aiToken.ownerTokenInvalid: the stored owner's token does not pass: the owner configures the external issuer again (takes the PIN)
server-access.aiToken.rateLimited: This session asked for tokens too often within a minute (at most {max}): try again later, or reuse the token already given
server-access.aiToken.selfAudience: An AI cannot be given a token for this Daisy itself: it reaches this Daisy with this turn's AI working credential (DAISY_AI_CREDENTIAL_FILE)
server-access.cliCredential.bad: The local credential file {file} is not right: delete it and start again to generate a new one
server-access.device.codeInvalid: The pairing code is wrong, used or expired: make a new one on the owner's Daisy ({command} pair, or Settings › Devices)
server-access.device.deviceFace: A paired device connects through the outside face only
server-access.device.deviceInvalid: This device's pairing is no longer valid (revoked, unused for too long, or not on the face it was paired on): pair it again
server-access.device.forgetNotDevice: Only a paired device can cancel its own pairing
server-access.device.pairFace: Pairing happens on the outside face only: open it with the link the owner gave you (or the outside face's address)
server-access.device.pairLocked: Too many wrong pairing codes from here; pairing from here is paused: try again in {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}
server-access.device.pairNoOutside: The outside face is off and there is no relay: paired devices connect through the outside face, so turn it on first (Settings › Faces and codes) or choose a relay (Settings › Relay); both take the PIN
server-access.device.tooMany: {max} devices are already paired: revoke the ones you no longer need first
server-access.device.tooManyOwner: {max} devices are already paired: revoke the ones you no longer need on the owner's Daisy first
server-access.external.badSetting: The outside face's settings are wrong; it was not turned on: {why}
server-access.external.failed: The outside face could not be turned on: {why}
server-access.external.failedSeeLog: The outside face could not be turned on ({code}); see the log for details
server-access.external.hostRequired: The listening address is an IP or host name (no port, not localhost)
server-access.external.noAddress: The outside face could not be turned on: this machine has no address {host}
server-access.external.plainHttp: Plain HTTP is allowed only on loopback, overlay or private network addresses (127/8, 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 100.64/10, ::1, fc00::/7); use TLS for any other address
server-access.guard.a2aOnly: This token does not stand for this Daisy's owner: the local API is not open to it (others call agents only through the A2A entry)
server-access.guard.channelAi: The AI's working credential cannot call this endpoint
server-access.guard.channelCli: The command line cannot do this (answering the AI's tool approvals and questions is only on the web page and paired devices)
server-access.guard.channelOther: This channel cannot call this endpoint
server-access.guard.credentialPagesOnly: Codes, pairing codes and device credentials are traded for credentials only on Daisy's own pages, not from an external interface's origin
server-access.guard.crossSite: Requests from other web pages are refused (cross-site protection)
server-access.guard.crossSiteExternal: Requests from other web pages are refused (cross-site protection); an external interface's page must be added by the owner to “Allowed external interface origins”
server-access.guard.crossSiteLocal: Requests from other web pages are refused (cross-site protection); an external interface's page can connect only through the outside face
server-access.guard.externalOff: This action is not turned on for the outside face: use it on this machine, or the owner turns it on in the settings (takes the PIN)
server-access.guard.hostNotAllowed: The requested host name is not this Daisy's address (DNS rebinding protection)
server-access.guard.insufficientScope: The credential's scope is not enough for this action
server-access.guard.letInScope: This action lets others in: the credential needs daisy:grant, and the PIN must be entered
server-access.guard.noCredential: No valid credential: open the web page with {command} open (it carries a one-time code); the command line uses the local credential in the data directory
server-access.guard.noInvoke: This token has no daisy:invoke: it cannot call agents
server-access.guard.notOwnSession: The AI's working credential can read only its own session
server-access.guard.pinRequired: This action needs the PIN: trade it for a PIN grant first, then retry with it
server-access.guard.pinUnavailable: The PIN is not available yet; this action cannot be done for now
server-access.guard.relayOff: The terminal, running commands and browsing directories are not offered through the relay: use them on this machine, or connect to the outside face directly over the overlay network
server-access.guard.routeNotDefined: This endpoint is not in the route table
server-access.guard.uiOriginToken: An external interface's page may carry only the token the external issuer signed for the owner; web sessions and the local credential cannot be used from another origin
server-access.guard.visitorsOnly: The A2A entry is for other agents to call: the owner's own credentials and the AI's working credential cannot use it (the owner uses the local API)
server-access.identityKey.notEd25519: The identity key {file} is not an Ed25519 private key: move it away and start again to generate a new one (AI credentials already signed become void)
server-access.issuer.credentials: The {what} may not carry a user name or password
server-access.issuer.fragment: The {what} may not carry a fragment (RFC 8414)
server-access.issuer.httpNeedsEnv: A plain-http issuer on a loopback address is allowed only with DAISY_ALLOW_HTTP_ISSUER=1 set (tests, same-machine setups)
server-access.issuer.httpSharedHost: Other people have accounts on this machine: a plain-http issuer on a loopback address could be impersonated by someone grabbing its port; https only
server-access.issuer.jwksNoKeys: The key set (JWKS) is malformed: no keys array
server-access.issuer.metaIssuerDiffers: The issuer in the metadata ({issuer}) differs from the configured issuer identifier
server-access.issuer.noSigningKey: The issuer's key set has no usable signing key (Ed25519, P-256, RSA of 2048 bits or more, with a kid)
server-access.issuer.noTokenEndpoint: The external issuer has no token endpoint (no token_endpoint in its metadata, and none was given when configuring it)
server-access.issuer.notHttps: The {what} must be an https address (plain http can be allowed only on the loopback addresses 127.0.0.1 / [::1])
server-access.issuer.ownerTokenInvalid: The owner's token does not pass: it must be an access token this issuer signed for the owner (ownerSubject), for this Daisy (audience), unexpired, without act, valid (exp - iat) for at most 24 hours
server-access.issuer.queryOrFragment: The {what} may not carry a query string or fragment (RFC 8414)
server-access.issuer.tooLarge: The answer of {origin} is too large (over {max} bytes)
server-access.letIn.pinChanged: The PIN was just set, changed or reset; this action did not take effect: enter the PIN again and retry
server-access.link.customCa: Issued by a certificate authority you named (the phone must trust it).
server-access.link.fingerprintThis: this one ({fingerprint}, also the one {command} access show prints)
server-access.link.notConnected: The relay is not connected now: it opens only once it is (see the status in Settings › Relay).
server-access.link.relayOperator.code: This link goes through a relay. The relay's operator can obtain a forged certificate and so get this one-time code and the web session opened with it — use it only if you trust this relay (for example one your team runs).
server-access.link.relayOperator.pair: This link goes through a relay. The relay's operator can obtain a forged certificate and so get the pairing code and this device's credential — use it only if you trust this relay (for example one your team runs).
server-access.link.selfSigned.code: The relay address has only a self-signed certificate now, so there is no link through the relay: enter the code on the other machine by hand. If the browser warns about the certificate, do not go on — do not click past the warning (you could not tell whether it is your own Daisy). To use a browser through the relay, turn on the certificate authority's certificate (ACME) in Settings › Relay and wait until it is issued.
server-access.link.selfSigned.pair: The relay address has only a self-signed certificate now, so there is no link or QR code through the relay: enter the pairing code on the device by hand. If the browser warns about the certificate, do not go on — do not click past the warning (you could not tell whether it is your own Daisy). To use a phone's browser through the relay, turn on the certificate authority's certificate (ACME) in Settings › Relay and wait until it is issued.
server-access.link.selfSignedListener: The outside face listens with a self-signed certificate: the browser will say the certificate is not trusted. Look at the certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint in the browser and go on only if it matches {which} and you are sure it is your own Daisy; if it does not match, stop.
server-access.pin.changedElsewhere: The PIN was just set, changed or reset elsewhere; it was not changed this time. Check the PIN status and retry.
server-access.pin.locked: Too many wrong PINs; locked: try again in about {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}. A forgotten PIN can be reset only on this machine: {command} pin reset --confirm (revokes every outside grant; then {command} pin set again).
server-access.pin.lockedNow: The PIN was entered wrong {n, plural, one {# time} other {# times}} in a row and is locked: try again in about {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}. A forgotten PIN can be reset only on this machine: {command} pin reset --confirm (revokes every outside grant; then {command} pin set again).
server-access.pin.notSet: No PIN is set yet (at least {min} characters). Set a PIN first: {command} pin set.
server-access.pin.oldRequired: A PIN is already set; changing it takes the old PIN first. A forgotten PIN can be reset only on this machine: {command} pin reset --confirm (revokes every outside grant; then {command} pin set again).
server-access.pin.setHint: Set a PIN first: {command} pin set
server-access.pin.unreadable: The stored PIN check value cannot be read (that database entry was changed or damaged); the PIN cannot be used for now. A forgotten PIN can be reset only on this machine: {command} pin reset --confirm (revokes every outside grant; then {command} pin set again).
server-access.pin.wrong: Wrong PIN. {left} more wrong tries lock it for a while. A forgotten PIN can be reset only on this machine: {command} pin reset --confirm (revokes every outside grant; then {command} pin set again).
server-access.port.givenInUse: Port {port} is in use (it was given, so it is not quietly changed): give another port, or drop it so Daisy picks one by its rule
server-access.port.noneFree: No free port between {from} and {to}: give one with DAISY_PORT
server-access.revoke.failed: Revoking “{kind}” ({name}) while resetting the PIN failed; the PIN was not reset{done}: {error}
server-access.secret.aclLoose: The credential file {file} is too open (accounts other than you, SYSTEM and Administrators can read it); refusing to start. Delete it and start again to generate a new one, or run {command} doctor to see how to tighten it
server-access.secret.empty: The credential file {file} is empty; delete it and start again to generate a new one. Refusing to start
server-access.secret.modeLoose: The credential file {file} has mode {mode}, too open: it must be 600 or stricter (chmod 600 {file}). Refusing to start
server-access.secret.notFile: The credential file {file} is not a regular file
server-access.secret.otherOwner: The credential file {file} is owned by uid {uid}, not the Daisy process's uid {own}; it may belong only to the system account that runs Daisy. Refusing to start
server-access.secret.symlink: The credential file {file} is a symbolic link; point to the real file directly
server-access.tls.certUnreadable: The outside face's certificate file {file} cannot be read ({error}). {redo}
server-access.tls.keyUnusable: The outside face's key file cannot be used: {error}. {redo}
server-access.tls.mismatch: The outside face's key {key} and certificate {cert} are not a pair. {redo}
server-access.tls.notFile: The outside face's certificate file {file} is not a regular file, refused; {redo}
server-access.tls.otherOwner: The outside face's certificate file {file} belongs to uid {uid}, not the account running Daisy (uid {own}), and other accounts can read it: refused; {redo}
server-access.tls.redo: Deleting {file} (and the other of tls-cert.pem / tls-key.pem in the same folder) and turning the outside face on again makes a new certificate — paired devices and callers that remember the old one will see the certificate change and must check the fingerprint again ({command} access show)
server-access.tls.short: The outside face's {what} in the data directory's keys/; no new certificate was made, see the log for details and what to do
server-access.tls.short.keyUnusable: key file cannot be used (owner, permissions or content)
server-access.tls.short.mismatch: key and certificate are not a pair
server-access.tls.short.notFile: certificate / key is not a regular file
server-access.tls.short.otherOwner: certificate / key belongs to another system account
server-access.tls.short.symlink: certificate / key file is a symbolic link
server-access.tls.symlink: The outside face's certificate file {file} is a symbolic link, refused; {redo}
server-access.token.badTtl: Write the lifetime as 7d, 12h, 30m or seconds: at least 1 minute, at most 90 days
server-access.token.contactGone: This contact was just removed: the token was not issued
server-access.token.notFound: No token with the number {jti}: look it up with {command} token list --state all
server-access.token.tooMany: {n} tokens are in force (limit {max}): revoke the ones you no longer need first ({command} token list, {command} token revoke)
server-access.token.warning: This token is shown only this once. Whoever has it can call your agents over A2A as this identity (call approval still applies): keep it like a password, never paste it into a chat or a code repository. Revoke it with {command} token revoke <jti> once it is no longer needed.
server-access.uiOrigin.credentials: “{origin}”: may not carry a user name or password
server-access.uiOrigin.httpsOnly: “{origin}”: only https:// is accepted (http:// on this machine's loopback)
server-access.uiOrigin.notConcrete: “{origin}” is not a concrete origin (* and null are not accepted)
server-access.uiOrigin.notUrl: “{origin}” is not a URL: write it as https://host[:port]
server-access.uiOrigin.path: “{origin}”: an origin has no path, query or #; write only scheme://host[:port]
server-access.uiOrigin.plainHttp: “{origin}”: plain http is allowed only on this machine's loopback (localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1]); other origins need https
server-access.web.codeInvalid: The one-time code is wrong, used or expired: run {command} open again on the machine Daisy runs on to get a new one
server-access.web.faceDown: This face is not listening yet
server-access.web.noOutside: The outside face is off and there is no relay: turn the outside face on or choose a relay first (Settings, takes the PIN)
server-access.web.passcodeLocal: A web page on this machine needs a code: run {command} open in a terminal and open the link it prints
server-access.web.passcodeRemote: Opening from another machine needs a code: run {command} open --external on the machine Daisy runs on and use the link or code it prints
